90% margin of error for Mining_Employment_Share, from Census's formula for a derived proportion (ACS handbook 2020, ch. 8, formula 6) using the S2403 MOEs. When it is at least the share itself, the share is not distinguishable from zero (Census's CV > 0.61 line) and the dashboard says so. Estimated proportion of school-age children (ages 5-17) living in families below the federal poverty line. Not a true poverty rate (Census): the first count includes only children related to the householder, in families in poverty; the second, all children 5-17 (foster children, other unrelated children and children in group quarters are in the second only). The dashboards label it "School-age children in poverty (Census est.)".
Total population of the SAIPE district behind the child poverty estimate (SAEPOVALL_PT); for a charter or early-childhood center, its surrounding district's. It sets the estimate's error band.

Low end of Census's approximate 90% range for Child_Poverty_Rate: rate x (1 - 1.645 x CV), floored at 0. CV is Census's median relative error for districts of that size (0.67 under 2,500 people down to 0.15 at 65,000+; "Quantifying Relative Error in the School District Estimates", revised 2025-12-17), which Census calls an approximate upper bound. Census publishes no margin of error for one district.
High end of the same range: rate x (1 + 1.645 x CV), capped at 1. See Child_Poverty_Low.
Release year of federal Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (SAIPE) data.
